text: Do long-distance relationships work? One of the most popular questions I get asked, along with how to forget your ex, do looks matter, and why do I always wear headphones? Hello. First of all, I'd like to say that I really enjoy your content and I agree with everything that you say. And it really made me want to ask you about your opinion on long-distance relationships. Since I've seen a lot of the people I know who are in these relationships, their relationships don't really last that long. Thank you. Thanks to you for the kind words and for the question. Your observation is correct. From experience, I can tell you that it is very, very difficult to make long-distance relationships work. In my opinion, LDRs can potentially work if these two conditions are met. First, you were already together in person before the distance started, meaning you already have a good relationship with all its attributes. There is trust, respect, empathy, you are compatible both physically and emotionally, meaning sex is good and you can spend time just enjoying talking about things. Second, there's a clear point when you will be back together. For example, you or she goes away for work or studies for three, maybe six months, and then you are back together again. That's pretty much it. In that case, yes, it's difficult, but it is manageable. But if the relationship started long-distance, I guess then the question is, can you even call it a relationship? Or if there is no clear timeline, you don't know when or even if you'll ever be together physically, that's not really a good relationship. That's a Russian roulette you're playing with your life. And the stats you are seeing with your friends, that's the result. We can speculate on what are the reasons, whether it is because good relationships need real presence or physical touch, whether it is because when you are not around, it's easy for each partner to have so-called wandering eyes. Reasons can be different, but experience shows distance makes it very easy for things to go wrong, including cheating. So my advice is straightforward. Simplify, don't complicate. There should be plenty of girls around you. Find the one you can spend time with both physically and emotionally. Hope that helps. My name is Ilyas Abdullin. Bye.
